id: title:Gilbert09:skip appsignal trace windows outside tracing retention

review.posthog_relevance: Warehouse ingestion stability for AppSignal connector, specifically handling documented terminal status codes (404, 422) as recoverable empty results rather than propagating exceptions.
review.reason: The change implements a bounded reliability improvement: it adds exception handling and status-code checks to the warehouse ingestion request, treating documented terminal statuses (404, 422) as recoverable empty results while still propagating unexpected errors. This preserves ingestion stability without changing broader system behavior. A parametrized test was added to verify the
review.uncertainty: The actual benefit depends on AppSignal returning these status codes for aged-out queries, which is not independently verified; the score reflects the implementation and test, not the realized outcome.

observations.limitations: Only supplied hunk IDs are cited. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds a try/except block around the HTTP request and its response processing; the original bare request and the subsequent `or []` are removed. The exception handler checks the HTTP status code and, if it is not 404 or 422, re-raises the exception. Otherwise, it treats the response as an empty list. This also adds a list comprehension to filter out non-dict rows.
observations.code_quote: if error.response is None or error.response.status_code not in (404, 422):
observations.posthog_connection: This could support AppSignal warehouse ingestion by treating documented terminal status codes (404, 422) as recoverable and returning an empty result instead of propagating an HTTP error, while still raising unexpected errors. This could help avoid ingestion failures when AppSignal returns these status codes for aged-out or unrunnable queries, and could preserve the ingestion job's

observations.behavior: Adds a parametrized test that mocks the warehouse connector to return HTTP status 404 or 422 and asserts that the ingestion result does not raise an exception and returns an empty row list.
observations.posthog_connection: This could support AppSignal warehouse ingestion by testing that the ingestion job does not fail when the warehouse returns documented terminal status codes, and that it returns an empty result instead of propagating an HTTP error. This could help preserve ingestion stability and avoid unnecessary failures when AppSignal returns these status codes for aged-out or unrunnable queries
